# pure_regex: Regular Expression Engine for Scryer Prolog and ISO Prolog

> A pure, ISO-compliant regular expression library for Scryer Prolog providing dual DCG non-terminal and direct character list (`chars`) matching interfaces across multiple 1:1 API-compatible engines (Rational Tree Automata, DCG, DFA).

## Overview & Key Entry Points

- **Primary Module**: `src/pure_regex.pl` (`pure_regex`) - Main entry point re-exporting Rational Tree Automaton by default.
- **Tree Automaton Engine**: `src/core/regexp_tree.pl` - Pure, deterministic `if_/3`-driven cyclic term finite state automaton matching engine.
- **DCG Engine**: `src/core/regexp_compile_dcg.pl` - Full-featured backtracking DCG engine with capturing groups, lookaheads, named groups, and inline flags.
- **DFA Engine**: `src/core/regexp_compile_dfa.pl` - Deterministic finite automaton execution.
- **Package Manifest**: `scryer-manifest.pl` - Bakage package definition (`pkg(pure_regex)`).

## Core Public API Interface

All engines maintain identical 1:1 API signatures:

### DCG Non-Terminal Predicates
- `re_match(Pattern, Match)//0` - Matches `Pattern` against DCG input, unifies matched `chars` with `Match`.
- `re_match(Pattern)//0` - Matches `Pattern` against DCG input without returning match slice.
- `re_match_groups(Pattern, Match, Groups)//0` - Matches `Pattern` and extracts positional capturing groups.
- `re_match_named(Pattern, Match, NamedMap)//0` - Matches `Pattern` and extracts named capturing groups.

### Direct List Matching Predicates
- `re_match(Pattern, Input)` - Anchored full match against `Input` character list (`chars`).
- `re_match(Pattern, Input, Rest)` - Matches prefix of `Input`, returning unparsed remainder `Rest`.
- `re_match(Pattern, Input, Rest, Options)` - Matches prefix with mode options (e.g. `[mode(dcg)]`, `[mode(tree)]`).
- `re_match_groups(Pattern, Input, Match, Groups)` - Direct match returning `Match` and `Groups` list.
- `re_match_named(Pattern, Input, Match, NamedMap)` - Direct match returning `Match` and named group list `[Name-Value, ...]`.

## Usage Examples

```prolog
:- use_module('src/pure_regex').

% Direct character list matching (Rational Tree engine default)
?- re_match("[a-z]+", "hello").
   true.

% Select DCG engine via mode option
?- re_match("[a-z]+", "hello", Rest, [mode(dcg)]).
   Rest = "".

% DCG non-terminal phrase matching
?- phrase(re_match("[0-9]+", Match), "12345").
   Match = "12345".

% Capturing positional groups
?- re_match_groups("(\\w+)@(\\w+)\\.(\\w+)", "user@domain.com", Match, Groups).
   Match = "user@domain.com", Groups = ["user", "domain", "com"].

% Named capture groups (requires mode(dcg))
?- re_match_named("(?P<year>\\d{4})-(?P<month>\\d{2})", "2026-08", Match, NamedMap).
   Match = "2026-08", NamedMap = ["year"-"2026", "month"-"08"].
```

## DCG Tokenizer & Lexer Recipe

`pure_regex` provides DCG non-terminals (`re_match//1`, `re_match//2`) for building declarative lexers:

```prolog
:- use_module(library(dcgs)).
:- use_module('src/pure_regex').

% Tokenize character list into structured AST tokens
tokenize(Input, Tokens) :-
    phrase(tokens(Tokens), Input).

tokens([]) --> ws.
tokens([Tok|Rest]) -->
    ws,
    token(Tok),
    !,
    tokens(Rest).

ws               --> re_match("\\s*", _).
token(ident(Id)) --> re_match("[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*", Id).
token(num(N))    --> re_match("-?[0-9]+", Chars), { number_chars(N, Chars) }.
token(str(S))    --> re_match("\"[^\"]*\"", S).
token(op(Op))    --> re_match("==|!=|<=|>=|[+\\-*/=<>]", Op).
```

## Engine Selection Guide

- **`tree` (Rational Tree Automaton, Default)**: Pre-compiles cyclic terms into a deterministic finite-state automaton. Fastest performance with no choicepoint generation for linear matching.
- **`dcg` (Backtracking DCG)**: Full-featured engine supporting capture groups (`re_match_groups/4`), named groups (`re_match_named/4`), lookaheads (`(?=...)`, `(?!...)`), and inline flags.
- **`dfa` (DFA Engine)**: Classical subset-construction deterministic finite automaton.

Developed collaboratively via human-guided agentic AI workflows, prompting agents to author and modify code, DCGs, tests, and comments under strict ISO Prolog purity guidelines and automated test suites.
